stem: A 9-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department after falling from a first-floor balcony. She is alert but distressed and complains of severe neck and back pain. She is immobilised on a spinal board with a hard cervical collar. What is the correct order of priorities in her initial assessment and management?

options.text: Disability or neurological status> Exposure> Breathing> Airway with Cervical Spine control > Circulation with haemorrhage control

explanation: In trauma, priorities follow the primary survey: Airway with cervical spine control, Breathing, Circulation with haemorrhage control, Disability, then Exposure (ABCDE).

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: The item is an ordering question, so the correct option is the one that matches standard trauma ABCDE priorities.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect order; disability and exposure are assessed later in the primary survey.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because exposure should not come before airway and breathing assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because airway with cervical spine control must be assessed before breathing.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: this is the standard ABCDE trauma sequence.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because breathing is assessed after airway, not before it.

Clinical scenario 3 - Anna

The following eight questions refer to Anna’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Immobilisation in children

Anatomical differences

SCIWORA

The triage nurse rushes into resuscitation with nine year old Anna and her parents. Anna is in her father’s arms. She has fallen from their first-floor balcony onto the lawn below. Her fall was not witnessed but heard by her parents, who immediately found her on her back in the garden crying. Rather than calling an ambulance, Anna’s parents brought her to emergency in their car.

The triage nurse is concerned Anna has fallen a significant height (greater than twice her standing height). Anna initially appears alert and very distressed. She is complaining of severe neck and back pain. Her respiratory rate is 26/min, saturations 100% in air, heart rate 110bpm, blood pressure 100/60. Based on her mechanism of injury, Anna was immediately secured on a spinal board with three straps, a hard cervical collar and sandbags.
